brief_corrections: geometry: the brief says 'all geometric functions and operators still missing (point-line ops, distance, containment, area, npoints, path ops, circle/polygon conversions, precise float formatting)'. Wrong: not one geometry function or operator fails in geometry.diff. 15 of 17 hunks (1334/1346 lines) are pure row REORDERS of unordered cross joins (verified by multiset comparison): PostgreSQL's nested loop puts the relation with fewer estimated rows (or the WHERE-filtered side) on the inner/materialized side, Gres always makes the first FROM item the outer loop. The other 12 lines are EXPLAIN const-fold deparse (circle(point(1,-2),1) vs '<(1,-2),1>'::circle).

box/polygon: 'type, operators, SP-GiST/GiST support' — the operators and the index DDL are correct; 277 of 340 lines are EXPLAIN plans that need Index Only Scan / Bitmap Heap+Index Scan / KNN Index Scan (planner-only). The single engine defect in box is box_in rejecting '(0,0)(0,100)' (comma between the two points is optional in PG's path_decode), which then cascades 5 rows through every later query.

datetime focus list: parsing edge cases, ISO 8601, EXTRACT returning numeric, make_* functions, age(), interval justification and pg_timezone_* all pass already. The dominant defect (1980 lines, 40% of the cluster) is that timestamp(p)/time(p)/interval(p) and interval field masks are parsed and DISCARDED (pgparser/src/parser.rs L651-663 comment says so); the second is that Datum::Timestamp/Timestamptz/PgDate are jiff civil types limited to years -9999..9999 (247 lines).

rangetypes: 97 of 124 lines are EXPLAIN (VERBOSE) 'Output:' lines that Gres does not print at all (plus PG's range-containment support-function rewrite) — cross-cluster EXPLAIN work, not a range-type gap.

file_stats.json 'explain_lines' undercounts: geometry has 12 EXPLAIN lines (listed as ~0), timestamptz 6, horology 12 (its 22 'explain-ish' includes 28 BETWEEN SYMMETRIC error lines that are a parser gap). timestamptz '40 gres-error lines' includes 5 INSERT errors that are one root (5/6-digit years).

multirangetypes: 40 of 186 lines are a cascade from one unparsed keyword (VARIADIC in a call argument), and 12 are GRANT/REVOKE ON TYPE + pg_type.typacl (privileges cluster), not multirange semantics.

roots.title: timestamp(p)/time(p)/interval(p) precision and interval field masks are parsed and discarded
roots.what_pg_does: Column typmod rounds on assignment (timestamp(2) column: 17:32:01.000001 -> 17:32:01, 17:32:01.999999 -> 17:32:02); typed literals interval(0) '1 day 01:23:45.6789' -> '1 day 01:23:46', interval '12:34.5678' minute to second(2) -> 00:12:34.57, interval '1 2:03:04.5678' day to second(2) -> 1 day 02:03:04.57, interval '2562047788:00:54.775807' second(2) -> 'interval out of range' with caret; casts f1::INTERVAL DAY TO MINUTE truncate to the field range ('1 day 02:03:00'), (f1 + '1 month')::INTERVAL MONTH::INTERVAL YEAR keeps only years; timestamp(2) without time zone 'now' literal rounds.
roots.what_gres_does: Precision dropped at parse time (crates/pgparser/src/parser.rs L651-663: 'Crabka stores every date/time value at microsecond resolution, so the precision is parsed and discarded'); ColumnType::Timestamp/Timestamptz/Time/Timetz/Interval carry no typmod (crates/pgtypes/src/datum.rs L719+); `interval '…' second(2)` / `day to second(2)` -> 'syntax error at position N: expected ; or end of input, found LParen'; `f1::INTERVAL DAY TO MINUTE` -> 'syntax error … found Ident("day")'; stored values keep full microseconds so every result set that prints the two fractional TIMESTAMP_TBL rows differs (columns widen, 65-row date_part tables change entirely).

fix_location.why: must carry Option<precision> (and interval field mask) like Varchar(Option<u16>) / Numeric(Option<Typmod>) so columns, casts and catalog atttypmod remember it; ~256 match sites reference these variants and need the payload
keep the (p) instead of discarding it; accept `field [TO field] (p)` after an interval literal and `INTERVAL field TO field [(p)]` in cast type names
apply the column's precision (round half-even on microseconds, PG AdjustTimestampForTypmod / AdjustIntervalForTypmod incl. field-mask truncation) on assignment; same in cast paths
explicit casts to typmod-bearing datetime types must round/truncate
pg_attribute.atttypmod for datetime types (raw precision; interval packs range mask) so format_type/\d print timestamp(2) without time zone
typmod-driven rounding helpers for interval seconds precision and field truncation

roots.size_rationale: Semantics are small (rounding + mask) but the ColumnType payload ripples through ~256 match sites in pgexec/pgtypes plus parser, catalog, format_type and deparse; several days of mechanical work.
roots.evidence: timestamp.diff H10: expected ' Mon Feb 10 17:32:01 1997 | 1997 | 2 | 10 | 17 | 32 | 1' / ' Mon Feb 10 17:32:02 1997 …' vs Gres ' Mon Feb 10 17:32:01.000001 1997 … | 1.000001' / ' … 17:32:01.999999 … | 1.999999'; interval.diff: 'SELECT interval '12:34.5678' minute to second(2);' expected ' 00:12:34.57', Gres 'ERROR:  syntax error at position 45: expected ; or end of input, found LParen'.
roots.oracle_facts: PG rounds fractional seconds half-away-from-zero at the typmod digit (AdjustTimestampForTypmod); typmod max 6; interval typmod packs field range mask + precision; `interval '1 2.345' day to second(2)` is 22007 'invalid input syntax for type interval: "1 2.345"' with caret; out-of-range after rounding is 'interval out of range' with caret at the literal.
roots.notes: Biggest root in the cluster (40%). timestamp/timestamptz/horology tables all use timestamp(2).

brief_corrections: jsonpath_encoding_2.out is the SKIP variant (\quit when getdatabaseencoding() is not UTF8/SQL_ASCII); Gres reports UTF8 and runs the whole file, so the diff (131) is 'everything after \endif'. The real target is jsonpath_encoding.out (UTF8): 108 changed lines vs the oracle run, all jsonpath-lexer unicode-escape handling (+ LINE cursor). Do not plan against _2.

xml/xmlmap: the CI oracle (self-check-serial) was built WITHOUT libxml: its results/xml.out is byte-identical to expected/xml_1.out and results/xmlmap.out to xmlmap_1.out. pg_regress picks the closest expected variant per file: xml is compared with xml.out (libxml behaviour; 1088 lines, vs 1327 against xml_1) because Gres already ships a native XML implementation (crates/pgtypes/src/xml.rs, 1798 lines, quick-xml tokenizer, libxml error wording); xmlmap is compared with xmlmap_1.out (131 lines vs 1329 against xmlmap.out). Both are legal pass conditions; the plan should aim xml at xml.out and xmlmap at xmlmap_1.out (unsupported-feature stubs) unless full SQL/XML mapping (XXL) is wanted. Oracle facts for xml must be read from expected/xml.out, not from the oracle .out.

Named arguments: the tests write `silent => true` and `vars => '{...}'` (=> notation), never `target := ...`. The parser itself rewrites named args to positional (crates/pgparser/src/parser.rs positional_from_named, ~line 3005) using a hard-coded table that knows only make_interval, so every other function fails with 42883 'function X does not support named arguments here'. Cost: 571 lines in jsonb_jsonpath (incl. the 149-line string-comparison matrix that uses vars => s2.j) + 22 in jsonb (jsonb_set_lax null_value_treatment =>).

'104 syntax error at or near … of jsonpath input' undercounts jsonpath: the largest sub-issue is numeric-literal lexing (exponent dropped: '1e1'::jsonpath prints 1, '1.2e3' prints 12; '00'/'0755' accepted; 0b/0o/0x and underscores refused; '1.' refused), then parenthesis canonicalisation (Gres wraps every binary op/comparison: `$"g"?((@ == 1))` vs `$"g"?(@ == 1)`), unary +/- folding into numeric literals, `$"a"` variable quoting, `last` scoping errors, string escapes (\v \x \u{...} unknown-escape), like_regex flag validation/canonical order, method arguments (.decimal(4,2), .time(6), .datetime("tmpl")), `(a > b).c`. All 909 lines are one grammar/printer root; 35 error blocks additionally lack the `LINE 1: … ^` cursor.

'.datetime(template) not supported' (69 lines) is only the visible tip: the jsonpath datetime family in jsonb_jsonpath is ~1265 lines (typed datetime items with tz flag, precision arguments, timestamp<->timestamptz conversion rules with 'cannot convert value from X to Y without time zone usage' + HINT, jsonb_path_*_tz variants, datetime comparisons in filters, template parsing errors).

sqljson '~142 explain-ish' lines are EXPLAIN VERBOSE `Output:` deparse lines (Result/Aggregate/WindowAgg over a syntactic plan), planner-only = 0. sqljson_jsontable '~0 explain-ish' is wrong: 56 lines of `Table Function Scan on "json_table"` + Output + Table Function Call, non-planner (needs EXPLAIN over a view to inline the view; Gres prints `Seq Scan on jsonb_table_view3`). jsonb explain_lines=30 in file_stats is really 36 planner-only lines (Bitmap Heap/Index Scan on a GIN index).
The per-file 'gres-error lines' counts in the brief (40/60/200/…) do not match either the diffs or file_stats.json (json: 182); they were not usable for attribution.

The XML row of PG_COMPAT_MATRIX / prior triage was not needed: Gres XML is not 'unsupported', it is a real implementation missing constructors (xmlelement/xmlpi/xmlroot/xmlforest/xmlagg), XPath (xpath/xpath_exists/xmlexists), XMLTABLE, SET XML OPTION and the SQL/XML mapping functions.

brief_corrections: Total changed lines for the 19 files is 5092 by the counting rule (per-file counts match the brief; the brief's per-file numbers were right, only my running sum matters here).

collate.utf8_1: the _1 variant is the 'skip when not UTF8' file (5 lines after \quit). Gres reports UTF8 so it runs the whole test; the real target is collate.utf8.out (340 lines: CREATE COLLATION provider=builtin, PG_C_UTF8, PG_UNICODE_FAST, collation-aware lower/upper/initcap/casefold and regex classes). Attribute the 168 lines to the builtin-collation root, not to a 'variant' quirk.

pg_lsn: the brief says 'arithmetic and aggregate'; the only remaining diff is one EXPLAIN (22 lines): join tree (planner) plus Sort Key/Group Key expression deparse (qualified Vars `i.i`, implicit `::text` casts, `Function Scan on generate_series k`).

inet: the brief says 'functions, operators, ordering, abbrev'; the only remaining diffs are EXPLAIN index/index-only scans with enable_seqscan off (planner-only), the row order those index scans imply, and one 4-line ORDER BY tie-order difference.

expressions: the brief says 'LIKE-related, boolean expr formatting'; the file's diffs are SQL-value functions with precision (current_time(4) etc.), current_catalog, typmods in casts/view columns, EXPLAIN VERBOSE Output, and CREATE OPERATOR shell operators (commutator/negator).

uuid: the 254 lines are a cascade of ONE defect (TEXT DEFAULT(now()) refused: pgtypes/src/cast.rs assignment_cast_allowed disallows non-string->string, whereas PostgreSQL treats I/O-conversion casts TO string types as assignment casts). The comment in cast.rs stating the opposite is wrong. Only 89 lines are uuidv7/uuid_extract_* functions.

The 'explain-ish' classifier over-counts for uuid/strings/case/collate: uuid EXPLAIN blocks are trivially syntactic (Aggregate -> Seq Scan -> Filter) and are lost only to the cascade; strings' 54 EXPLAIN lines are SIMILAR TO -> POSIX regex constant folding (expression preprocessing, not cost-based planning); case's 24 EXPLAIN lines are constant folding to 'Result / One-Time Filter: false'; collate's 12 are Sort Key COLLATE decoration. I count none of these as planner-only.

regex: 63 of the 445 lines are planner-only (regex prefix -> Index Cond on pg_proc_proname_args_nsp_index). The other 381 need a PostgreSQL-compatible ARE engine; the Rust `regex` crate is used on the raw pattern today (pgexec/src/regexp_fn.rs compile_pattern), so back-references, lookaround, \m \M \Y, POSIX longest-match, ARE non-greedy semantics, `\x7fffffff` rejection and 'regular expression is too complex' cannot be patched in.

encoding + conversion: both files depend on regress.so C functions (test_bytea_to_text, test_mblen_func, test_text_to_wchars, test_enc_setup, test_enc_conversion) AND on text values that hold invalid UTF-8 / NUL bytes and on the whole PostgreSQL encoding-conversion library (EUC_JIS_2004, SHIFT_JIS_2004, MULE_INTERNAL, KOI8R, GB18030, LATIN1, EUC_*). This is far larger than 'convert/convert_from/convert_to and pg_conversion' suggests.

The 'physical row order after UPDATE' root (arrays H8, case H5) is cross-cluster: PostgreSQL's heap moves an updated row to the end of the seq-scan order; Gres keeps its rowid. It probably costs many more lines in other clusters.

The numeric H1 (60 lines) and case H2/H3 (60 lines) row-order differences are cross-join ORDER-less outputs whose order comes from PostgreSQL's cost-based join order (the filtered / smaller relation becomes the outer). Counted planner-only, though a 'filtered relation outer' heuristic would match both.

brief_corrections: file_stats 'gres-error lines' counts are far below reality for cascade files: index_including has 94 error-carrying lines, not 30; create_index 148, not 120; brin_multi 48, not 20 (the classifier undercounts). Changed-line totals per file are correct (5530 in this cluster).

compression_1 is compared against the no-lz4 variant only because pg_regress picks the closest expected file; Gres may target either compression.out (lz4 present) or compression_1.out (lz4 absent). The no-lz4 variant is the cheaper target: it needs 'compression method lz4 not supported' + DETAIL, never actual lz4.

'partial indexes (declared unsupported)' in the brief is accurate, but the CREATE INDEX grammar already parses WHERE and stores the predicate text; the refusal is in exec.rs::index_key_columns, not the parser.

The brief lists 'INCLUDE columns' as an execution gap; it is refused at exec.rs (CREATE INDEX) and is a *syntax error* in the constraint spellings (CREATE TABLE ... UNIQUE(...) INCLUDE(...), ALTER TABLE ADD PRIMARY KEY (...) INCLUDE (...)) — parser work is needed too.

hash_func expected outputs are '(0 rows)' consistency checks (hashX(v) == hashXextended(v,0) and != hashXextended(v,1)); exact hash values are only observable indirectly (partition hashing elsewhere). Gres already ports lookup3 in crates/pgexec/src/partition/hash.rs; the gap is SQL-callable wrappers for every type, not the algorithm.

random: Gres already runs xoroshiro128** with PG's range/rejection logic (math_fn.rs::Prng); the divergences are seeding (pg_prng_seed splitmix64, pg_prng_fseed constant), random_normal missing, random(int8,int8)/numeric variants and the negative INT64_MIN literal. The KS-test 'f' results (6 lines) are NOT explained by PRNG quality; a repro is needed (candidates: row_number() OVER () ordering over an ORDER BY'd CTE, or numeric/float mixing in the plpgsql body).

tablesample: 'expected exact rows given seeds' additionally requires emulating heap page layout (8 KiB pages, tuple headers, fillfactor) because SYSTEM samples blocks and BERNOULLI iterates (block, offset) with a per-block PRNG stream; PG's PRNG alone is not enough.

The tablespace file also carries a leaked TEMP table 'test_io_local' created by stats.sql (ALTER TABLE ... SET TABLESPACE regress_tblspace) that should have died with that session — a temp-relation lifecycle defect outside this cluster (session.rs::drop_temp_relations/terminate) that costs ~20 tablespace lines.

brin/brin_bloom first failures are not BRIN at all: an INSERT ... SELECT ... FROM tenk1 ORDER BY ... LIMIT trips the hard-coded 16 MiB sort budget in exec.rs::key_source_rows (uses scanner::BLOCKING_QUERY_MEMORY, not the configured 20 MiB budget, and materializes all keyed rows instead of top-k). This is a cross-cluster producer (21 diffs mention it).

brief_corrections: partition_join and partition_prune are NOT cascades. 3611/4199 (86%) of partition_join and 2866/4035 (71%) of partition_prune are EXPLAIN plans over tables that exist (prt1/prt2/plt*/pht*/lp/rlp/mc2p/ab/hp...). The expression-partition-key cascade is 561 lines (prt1_e/prt2_e/prt1_m/prt2_m/plt1_e/pht1_e) in partition_join and 589 lines (mc3p x2, iboolpart, coll_pruning_multi) in partition_prune. The prior '55 / 72 relation does not exist' figures were statement counts inside those cascades, not the line cost. The first failing statement in both files is the very first EXPLAIN (Append/Hash Join shape), not a DDL statement.

tableoid is no longer the gate for inherit: `SELECT relname, a.* FROM a, pg_class WHERE a.tableoid = pg_class.oid` now differs only in row order (heap order after UPDATE). inherit is gated on (a) DROP TABLE ... CASCADE not dropping inheritance children (orphans -> 42P07 'already exists' -> every later create/alter/\d on those names goes wrong), (b) NOT NULL and CHECK constraints not being catalog objects with inheritance metadata, and (c) INHERITS refusing a locally redeclared inherited column ('column "x" specified more than once').

The ordering defect is two-fold, not one: inheritance::children_of returns KV key order (four-byte length prefix -> siblings sort by name length first) while PostgreSQL orders inheritance children by OID (creation order); partition::partitions_of/leaves_of/descendants sort by RelationName (lexical) while PostgreSQL scans partitions in PartitionDesc bound order (list values ascending with NULL/default last, range lower bounds ascending, hash by modulus/remainder). Both must change; the 'name length' note is right only for plain INHERITS children.

Two failures in inherit are not fixable in this cluster: `list_parted` and `range_parted` already exist when inherit runs (a previous schedule file leaves them behind), so `create table list_parted (a varchar) partition by list (a)` is 42P07 and its bounds then coerce to the stale table's int key ('invalid input syntax for type integer: "ab"'). 16 lines depend on whichever file leaks them.
The gres-error line counts in the brief were capped at 100 for partition_join/partition_prune/indexing/inherit; file_stats.json says 63/123/148/238.

The hash-partition row placement diffs in partition_prune (hp, hp_prefix_test) are not a hash-routing bug: Gres's lookup3 port is byte-exact, but the test tables are declared with the custom hash opclasses part_test_int4_ops / part_test_text_ops from test_setup (part_hashint4_noop = value+seed, part_hashtext_length = length). Gres parses PartitionKeyElem.opclass and then drops it (partition::Scheme keeps only key names), so rows are routed with the builtin hash and land in different partitions.

Prior 'inherit +57 accepted when binding began reporting unresolvable columns' is no longer visible; the surviving 42703s in inherit come from RENAME COLUMN not recursing to children (`column "aa" does not exist`) and from a spurious rename refusal ('a stored view's definition references a relation this catalog cannot resolve').

roots.title: Cost-based plan shapes in EXPLAIN (join method/order, index and bitmap scans, Memoize/Materialize, Merge Append, partitionwise join/aggregate, Partial/Finalize, parallel Gather, equivalence-class Sort Key pruning, cost-ordered quals)
roots.what_pg_does: Chooses Hash Join / Merge Join / Nested Loop per partition pair under Append (enable_partitionwise_join), HashAggregate vs GroupAggregate with Partial/Finalize under Append (enable_partitionwise_aggregate), Index/Index Only/Bitmap scans when indexes exist or enable_seqscan is off, Merge Append vs Append by pathkeys, Memoize/Materialize on inner sides, Gather with Parallel Seq Scan when parallel GUCs are set, and prints them with the actual-rows counters under EXPLAIN ANALYZE.
roots.what_gres_does: explain.rs is a syntactic AST walk: every join is 'Nested Loop' with a single 'Join Filter', every scan is 'Seq Scan on <parent>', aggregates are one HashAggregate/Aggregate over the scan, no index is ever consulted (module docs say so).

fix_location.why: the renderer must consume a real plan tree from a cost-based planner instead of walking the AST
EXPLAIN must plan against the catalog (indexes, partition descriptors, statistics), not the bare statement
the executor has to run the chosen join method (hash/merge/memoize) so ANALYZE counters match
row estimates and join-order choice need ANALYZE statistics

roots.size_rationale: Requires a PostgreSQL-faithful cost model, path generation (partitionwise join/aggregate, Merge Append, parallel paths, min/max InitPlan rewrite) and an executor that runs those node types; this is the shared PLANNER programme, not partition-specific work.
roots.notes: Direct lines: partition_join 3613, partition_aggregate 1076, partition_prune 519, inherit 491, indexing 36. A further 1,182 cost-based lines are hidden behind producer roots and are charged there (see each root's notes).

roots.title: Partition-aware plan tree in EXPLAIN: Append over leaf scans in bound order, static and run-time partition pruning, EXPLAIN EXECUTE/ANALYZE over partitions, bound-expression deparse

roots.title: Expression partition keys (PARTITION BY RANGE/LIST/HASH over expressions, with COLLATE and opclass)

roots.title: Partitioned index inheritance: pg_inherits rows for indexes, ALTER INDEX ATTACH PARTITION, ON ONLY, INVALID state, auto-attach on ATTACH/CREATE INDEX, DROP INDEX rules, index-backed constraint metadata on partitions
roots.what_pg_does: A CREATE INDEX on a partitioned table creates a relkind 'I' index with relhassubclass, recursively creates or attaches matching partition indexes (match by key columns/expressions/predicate/collation/opclass; 'Another index is already attached for partition'), records pg_inherits(inhrelid=child index, inhparent=parent index); CREATE INDEX ... ON ONLY leaves the parent INVALID until every partition has an attached valid index; ALTER INDEX p ATTACH PARTITION c validates ('is not an index', 'cannot attach index ... as a partition of index ...' + DETAIL 'The index definitions do not match.' / 'Index "x" is not an index on any partition of table "t".' / belongs-to-constraint mismatch), sets validity upward; DROP INDEX on a partition index is refused 'cannot drop index idxpart1_a_idx because index idxpart_a_idx requires it' + HINT 'You can drop index idxpart_a_idx instead.'; pg_indexes/pg_get_indexdef print 'ON ONLY public.idxpart' for partitioned indexes; \d+ on a partition index prints 'Partition of: idxparti' / 'No partition constraint'; \d prints 'INVALID' after invalid indexes; index-backed constraints on partitions carry conislocal=f, coninhcount=1, connoinherit as parent, 'cannot drop inherited constraint'; ALTER TABLE ... ATTACH/DETACH on an index says '"idxpart_c" is not a partitioned table' / DETAIL 'This operation is not supported for partitioned indexes.'; CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on a partitioned table is refused; DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY of a partitioned index is refused; a CIC that fails (division by zero) leaves an INVALID index; ALTER TABLE ... REPLICA IDENTITY USING INDEX flags indisreplident.
roots.what_gres_does: Clones partition indexes (cloned_partition_index) without recording inheritance: pg_inherits_rows only walks tables, so inhparent is always NULL and relhassubclass=f for the parent index; ALTER INDEX ... ATTACH PARTITION is a syntax error ('expected Keyword(Set), found Ident("attach")'); indexdef omits ON ONLY; no INVALID state (indisvalid always t); \d+ of a partition index shows no columns and no 'Partition of:'; DROP INDEX on a partition index succeeds; constraint rows on partitions have conislocal=t/coninhcount=0 and duplicated rows appear for idxpart1_pkey; DETAIL says 'not supported for indexes'; CIC failure is not detected; REPLICA IDENTITY USING INDEX is an unsupported ALTER subcommand.

roots.title: Physical row order after UPDATE (updated tuple versions come last in a heap scan)

roots.what_gres_does: Rows keep their rowid position; the updated row is returned in its original place ('zzzzzz' first).

fix_location.why: to emulate heap placement the new version needs a fresh, larger scan key (delete+insert semantics)
the memory notes record a timestamp-domain rowid contract that any change must respect

roots.size_rationale: Storage-order semantics with cross-cutting risk (row identity, indexes, FK, triggers); PostgreSQL's page-local placement can only be approximated (append-at-end is exact for single-page tables).
roots.notes: Only 8 lines here but the same effect appears in many other files; flagged for the storage cluster.

roots.title: Scan and enumeration order of partitions (bound order) and inheritance children (OID order)

fix_location.why: sort by Bound (list values, range lower bound, hash remainder), default last, depth-first per parent

consumes leaves_of; must keep bound order for the executor and EXPLAIN alias numbering

roots.size_rationale: Ordering rule in three functions; prerequisite for Append alias numbering and pg_partition_tree order.

brief_corrections: privileges is NOT '~0 explain-ish': 96 changed lines are EXPLAIN plans in the leaky-view section (atest12/atest12v/atest12sbv); they are planner-only (Index Scan/Hash Join/Materialize) once the `<<<`/`>>>` operator lexing gap is fixed.

rowsecurity's '~946 explain-ish' lines are mostly NOT planner-only: ~628 lines sit in EXPLAIN hunks but only ~66 need a cost-based planner (Hash Join, Index Scan using uaccount_pkey/category_pkey, Materialize). The remainder is deterministic shape that a syntactic explain.rs can produce: RLS USING quals inside Filter, Append over inheritance/partition children with t1_1 aliases, InitPlan/SubPlan (hashed), LockRows, view expansion, EXPLAIN EXECUTE, permission checks, `Result / One-Time Filter: false`.

'database (backslash-c reconnect)' does not occur: database.diff (10 lines, one hunk, full cascade) is CREATE/ALTER/DROP DATABASE grammar + tenant-lifecycle refusal + REASSIGN OWNED + a superuser `UPDATE pg_database SET datacl = array_fill(makeaclitem(...))`.

misc (231), misc_functions (767) and namespace (29) are only nominally security: their bulk is SQL-function composite/functional notation (`$1.name`, `name(p.hobbies)`, `hobbies_r.name%TYPE`), admin/file/WAL functions, C-language regress.so functions, and the GUC-runtime scope / routine-namespace defects.

The `bar\ttrue` / `invalid command \.` lines in privileges are a cascade of the preceding COPY permission failure (psql never entered copy mode), not a psql/protocol root; PG's own failing COPYs in that file carry no data lines.

rowsecurity `SELECT * FROM t1 FOR SHARE` -> `relation "t1" does not exist` comes from the locking-select path (execute_locking_select_with_scalar_actor) resolving the name without search_path, an inheritance/locking defect, not RLS.

Gres user routines have no schema at all: crates/pgparser/src/parser.rs routine_name() refuses any non-`public` qualifier with 3F000, routine.rs resolves signature composite types only in `public`, and CREATE FUNCTION under a non-public search_path lands in public. Several 'does not exist' errors in privileges (testns.foo), rowsecurity (rls_t rowtype, op_leak lookup) and namespace (fn(i)) stem from that, not from privileges.
file_stats.json error_lines for privileges is 622, not 200 as the brief says; the brief's per-file numbers appear to be capped.

roots.title: pg_auth_members with grantor / ADMIN / INHERIT / SET options and PG16+ role administration semantics
roots.what_pg_does: Membership rows carry (roleid, member, grantor, admin_option, inherit_option, set_option). GRANT r TO m [WITH ADMIN|INHERIT|SET {OPTION|TRUE|FALSE}, ...] [GRANTED BY x]; REVOKE [ADMIN|INHERIT|SET OPTION FOR] r FROM m [GRANTED BY x] [CASCADE|RESTRICT]. Grantor is inferred (must hold ADMIN; superuser grants are recorded as bootstrap superuser oid 10). Errors: 'ADMIN option cannot be granted back to your own grantor'; 'dependent privileges exist' + HINT 'Use CASCADE to revoke them too.'; 'permission denied to grant role "x"' DETAIL 'Only roles with the ADMIN option on role "x" may grant this role.'; 'permission denied to grant privileges as role "x"' DETAIL 'The grantor must have the ADMIN option on role "x".'; NOTICE 'role "m" has already been granted membership in role "r" by role "g"'; WARNING 'role "m" has not been granted membership in role "r" by role "g"'; 'permission denied to set role "x"' when SET option is absent; SET ROLE suspends the session user's ADMIN rights while SECURITY DEFINER conveys them; DROP ROLE fails with 'role "x" cannot be dropped because some objects depend on it' DETAIL 'privileges for membership of role m in role r'; CREATE/ALTER/DROP GROUP synonyms ('ALTER GROUP g ADD/DROP USER u' with DETAIL 'Only roles with the ADMIN option on role "g" may add or drop members.'); role_has_privs_of honours INHERIT option and rolinherit; ALTER TABLE ... OWNER TO needs 'must be able to SET ROLE "x"'; predefined roles pg_read_all_data, pg_write_all_data, pg_read_all_settings, pg_read_all_stats, pg_monitor, pg_signal_backend, pg_maintain, pg_database_owner exist ('role "pg_database_owner" cannot have explicit members' / 'cannot be a member of any role'); pg_has_role answers from memberships; information_schema.enabled_roles/applicable_roles project them; createrole_self_grant GUC; CREATEROLE creator receives implicit ADMIN OPTION on roles it creates.
roots.what_gres_does: crabka_pgcatalog stores a membership as a bare key `catalog/role_membership/<member>/<role>` with no payload; parser eat_with_admin_option accepts only WITH ADMIN OPTION and the executor discards it (exec.rs GrantRoles comment); GRANTED BY / CASCADE / WITH INHERIT|SET TRUE|FALSE / REVOKE INHERIT|SET OPTION FOR are syntax errors ('expected ; or end of input, found Ident("granted")', 'expected `admin`, found Ident("inherit")', 'expected a role name, found Keyword(Set)'); CREATE GROUP -> 'expected Keyword(Table), found Keyword(Group)'; ALTER GROUP -> 'unexpected token after ALTER: Keyword(Group)'; ADMIN-option checks admit only superusers ('permission denied to grant role "regress_group"' for a legitimate direct manager); predefined roles are absent ('role "pg_read_all_data" does not exist', 'object "pg_read_all_settings" does not exist' on SET ROLE); pg_has_role returns t/t/t; pg_auth_members relation does not exist; ownership transfer never checks SET ROLE ability.

PASSWORD storage in pg_authid.rolpassword: plaintext hashed with SCRAM-SHA-256 (iterations from scram_iterations GUC, output 'SCRAM-SHA-256$4096:<salt>$<storedkey>:<serverkey>'), already-encrypted MD5/SCRAM values stored verbatim (MD5 with WARNING 'setting an MD5-encrypted password' + DETAIL/HINT), empty string -> NOTICE 'empty string is not a valid password, clearing password', >512 bytes -> 'encrypted password is too long' DETAIL 'Encrypted passwords must be no longer than 512 bytes.', variant password_1: 'password encryption failed: unsupported' for plaintext under md5; brief_corrections: select_views is not primarily a security-barrier/leaky-view file: 901 of its 1036 lines are a cross-file cascade of create_view's `CREATE VIEW iexit` failing, because Gres calls the C-language function interpt_pp while deriving the view's column types (routine.rs `callable()` reached from `inline_scalar_call` during describe). Only 20 lines are NOTICE-count (qual ordering) and 113 are EXPLAIN plans.

updatable_views' '~340 explain-ish' understates the planner share: ~405 lines are EXPLAIN blocks (every EXPLAIN UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE/INSERT through a view also fails today with 'relation does not exist' because describe_statement only resolves tables). 264 lines are auto-updatable-view rewrite defects (viewwrite.rs), 183 are rule-system, 173 are ALTER VIEW ... ALTER COLUMN SET DEFAULT.

rules is 58% a single block that has nothing to do with CREATE RULE: `SELECT viewname, definition FROM pg_views WHERE schemaname='pg_catalog'` (1437 lines; 80 system views deparsed byte-exactly, plus the two pg_settings rules from pg_rules). Gres returns 0 rows because its system views are virtual and pg_rules does not exist.
The brief's 'gres-error lines' counts undercount by design; e.g. rules has 138 error lines by the classifier but the rule blocks they open cost ~805 lines.

pgcatalog's ViewOptions doc says security_barrier is 'recorded and inert for a structural reason'; the tests show it is observable: NOTICE ordering from leaky functions differs, and UPDATE/DELETE through a barrier view in Gres evaluates the caller's leaky qual on rows the barrier hides (updatable_views 'snooped value: Dick').

The compat matrix declares RULE a Non-goal (bounded refusal 0A000 for DROP/ALTER RULE; CREATE RULE is not even parsed — 'rule' is not a keyword). Sized here as XXL: parser + pg_rewrite catalog + query rewriter + pg_rules/pg_get_ruledef/\d+ Rules + interaction with auto-updatable views, ON CONFLICT, MERGE, RETURNING, permissions.
matview's `FROM mvtest_mvschema.mvtest_tvm` rendering after SET SCHEMA is not only an ALTER ... SET SCHEMA gap: it needs bound view storage (relation identity, qualify-if-not-visible), i.e. root R2.
The 'variant expected file' list in the brief does not affect this cluster (none of the five files use a _1/_2 variant).

roots.title: Rewrite rule system: CREATE/DROP/ALTER RULE, pg_rewrite, rewriter, pg_rules, pg_get_ruledef, \d+ Rules
roots.what_pg_does:
CREATE [OR REPLACE] RULE name AS ON {SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE} TO rel [WHERE qual] DO [ALSO|INSTEAD] {NOTHING | cmd | (cmd; cmd; ...)} stores a pg_rewrite row; the rewriter expands DO ALSO/INSTEAD actions (NEW/OLD substituted, qualified rules add the qual, unqualified INSTEAD suppresses the original, rules fire in name order, multi-action rules run each command, cascaded rules on the action's target fire recursively), returns the last action's RETURNING for DO INSTEAD, and reports rows via `VALUES(old.*, 'old')` DO ALSO actions. Views with rules: an unconditional DO INSTEAD rule makes a view insertable/updatable in information_schema; a conditional one refuses auto-update with DETAIL 'Views with conditional DO INSTEAD rules are not automatically updatable.'; `INSERT with ON CONFLICT clause cannot be used with table that has INSERT or UPDATE rules`; `cannot execute MERGE on relation "rule_merge1"` DETAIL 'MERGE is not supported for relations with rules.'; ALTER TABLE ENABLE/DISABLE/ENABLE REPLICA RULE and session_replication_role decide firing; DROP RULE, ALTER RULE ... RENAME TO (`rule "insertrule" for relation "rule_v1" does not exist`, `rule "_RETURN" for relation "rule_v1" already exists`, `renaming an ON SELECT rule is not allowed`), COMMENT ON RULE (`rule "rtest_v1_bad" for relation "rtest_v1" does not exist`), `cannot drop rule _RETURN on view rules_fooview because view rules_fooview requires it` HINT 'You can drop view rules_fooview instead.', `relation "rules_fooview" cannot have ON SELECT rules` DETAIL 'This operation is not supported for tables.'/'partitioned tables.'; `relation "old" in FOR UPDATE clause not found in FROM clause` for `for update of old`; main-query relation permissions checked before rule-action relations; pg_rules.definition and \d+ 'Rules:' print `CREATE RULE r AS
    ON UPDATE TO public.t DO INSTEAD  UPDATE ... ` / `r1 AS
    ON UPDATE TO rules_src DO  INSERT INTO rules_log (f1, f2, tag, id) VALUES (old.f1,old.f2,'old'::text,DEFAULT), ...` (ruleutils layout incl. `NOTIFY`, WITH-CTE actions, `AS trgt` aliases, multiassignment `SET (f2[1], f1, tag) = ( SELECT ...`, `INSERT INTO hat_data (hat_name, hat_color) VALUES (new.hat_name, new.hat_color) ON CONFLICT(hat_name COLLATE "C" bpchar_pattern_ops) WHERE (hat_color = 'green'::bpchar) DO NOTHING RETURNING hat_data.hat_name, ...`); pg_get_ruledef(oid, true) of a view's _RETURN rule prints `CREATE RULE "_RETURN" AS
    ON SELECT TO tt23v DO INSTEAD  SELECT ...`.
roots.what_gres_does: CREATE RULE is a parse error: `syntax error at position 7: expected Keyword(Table), found Ident("rule")` (`rule` is not a keyword; CREATE OR REPLACE RULE fails at `Or`). DROP RULE / ALTER RULE ... RENAME hit the bounded non-goal refusal: `ERROR: the legacy rewrite rule system is not supported` (0A000). COMMENT ON RULE: `syntax error at position 29: expected Keyword(Is), found Keyword(On)`. ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE RULE: `syntax error ...: expected `trigger`, found Ident("rule")`. `SELECT ... FROM pg_rules` -> `relation "pg_rules" does not exist`. pg_get_ruledef returns NULL (catalog_fn NullDef). \d+ prints no Rules section. Views the tests make updatable via rules are refused with the auto-updatable messages; tables whose rules redirect rows keep the rows.

fix_location.why: No CREATE RULE grammar; DROP/ALTER RULE are matched by refusal_tokens_match into Statement::CompatibilityRefusal
Replace the refusal variants with real CreateRule/DropRule/AlterRule/CommentOnRule/EnableRule statements

pg_get_ruledef(oid[, pretty]) must deparse rules incl. _RETURN

roots.title: Views and matviews stored as SQL text instead of a bound query tree
roots.what_pg_does: CREATE VIEW freezes the query: `*` expanded, every column reference bound to (relation oid, attnum), pg_depend rows per referenced column; ALTER TABLE RENAME / RENAME COLUMN / ADD COLUMN never change what a view returns; pg_get_viewdef regenerates names from the catalog and adds column-alias lists when a table's column names no longer match the view's (`FROM tt2 JOIN tt3 tt3(ax, b, c) USING (b, c)`, `tt11 tt11(x, y, z_1)`, `"?dropped?column?" AS f3`), uniquifies clashing aliases (`FROM a1 a1_1 WHERE a1.f1 = a1_1.x1`), qualifies relations not visible on search_path (`FROM mvtest_mvschema.mvtest_tvm`); DROP COLUMN refuses only for columns the view actually references (`cannot drop column f3 of table tt14t because other objects depend on it` DETAIL `view tt14v depends on column f3 of table tt14t`); REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW keeps working after the base column is renamed.
roots.what_gres_does: pgcatalog `View.definition: String` / `MaterializedView.definition: String` hold the AS text; exec.rs `rename_table_view_ops` rewrites the text by a token walk and refuses everything else: `cannot rename relation "testviewschm2.a1": a stored view references it in a position this catalog cannot rewrite`; `alter table tt3 rename c to d` -> `cannot rename column "c" ...: a stored view's definition references a relation this catalog cannot resolve`; `alter table tt7 drop column zz` refused although the views were created before zz existed (the star is re-expanded at drop time); REFRESH mvtest_mv_v -> `column "i" does not exist`; alias lists and a1_1 uniquification never appear.

fix_location.why: Store a resolved query (relation ids + attnums + original aliases + column alias lists) instead of text

fix_location.symbol: Statement::CreateView arm (~1070) with validate_view_definition/describe_query_expr; rename_table_view_ops (~30420); rewrite_view_relation_name; ALTER TABLE RENAME COLUMN / DROP COLUMN dependency checks (dependent view scan near 30380)

Consumes the stored text; must consume the bound tree

roots.size_rationale: Changes the catalog representation every view reader uses (scan, viewwrite, viewdef, deps, refresh, information_schema, psql \d+); every rename/add/drop column path must update or consult the bound tree.

roots.title: pg_get_viewdef / \d+ deparse must follow ruleutils.c exactly
roots.what_pg_does: Qualifies every Var when the query has more than one RTE (`SELECT tt2.b, tt3.c, tt2.a, tt3.ax`), prints USING-merged output columns unqualified and with `x AS a` when renamed; expands NATURAL JOIN to `JOIN tt3 USING (b, c)`, empty NATURAL to `CROSS JOIN tt6`, empty NATURAL LEFT to `LEFT JOIN tt6 ON TRUE`; whole-row vars as `i.*::int8_tbl`, `ROW(i.*::int8_tbl)::nestedcomposite AS "row"`, `r.*::record AS r`, `(cte.r).column2`; `(x, y) <> ALL (...)` not `ROW(x, y)`; pretty mode keeps precedence-required parens (`(x + y) * z`, `x + (y # z)`, `x > y AND (y > z OR x > z)`); unknown literals as `'foo'::text`, casts with typmod `'abc'::character varying(3)`; bare VALUES view as `SELECT column1, column2 FROM (VALUES (1,2)) "*VALUES*"`; `LATERAL ( VALUES (i.*::int8_tbl)) ss`; `'foo'::text = ANY ((( SELECT ARRAY[...] AS "array"))::text[])`; RTE_FUNCTION forms `COALESCE(1, 2) c(c)`, `COLLATION FOR ('x'::text) col(col)`, `CURRENT_DATE d(d)`, `LOCALTIMESTAMP(3) t(t)`, `CAST(1 + 2 AS integer) i4(i4)`, `CAST((1 + 2)::bigint AS bigint) i8(i8)`; SQL special syntaxes `AT TIME ZONE`, `EXTRACT(day FROM now())`, `OVERLAPS`, `IS [NFKC] NORMALIZED`, `NORMALIZE(x, NFKD)`, `OVERLAY(... PLACING ... FROM 2 FOR 3)`, `POSITION(('foo'::text) IN ('foobar'::text))`, `SUBSTRING(... SIMILAR ... ESCAPE ...)`, `"substring"('foo'::text, 'oo'::text)`, `TRIM(BOTH ' '::text FROM ...)`, `( SELECT "current_date"."current_date" FROM CURRENT_DATE "current_date"("current_date")) AS cd2` etc.
roots.what_gres_does: viewdef.rs deparses the raw parse tree: `Ctx.qualifier` exists only for a sole FROM item so multi-relation queries print bare names; NATURAL JOIN printed as written; `x AS a` missing; `operand_text` never adds parens in pretty mode so `(x + y) * z` prints as `x + y * z` (semantically wrong text); `ROW(x, y) <> ALL`; `'abc'::text::character varying`; whole-row prints `i`, `(r).column2`; VALUES view prints `VALUES (1,2);`; special syntaxes not parsed at all (see parser root).

roots.title: ALTER VIEW ... ALTER COLUMN SET/DROP DEFAULT and view defaults on INSERT/MERGE through the view
roots.what_pg_does: Stores a default on a view column; INSERT/MERGE INTO view supplies the view default (over the base table's) for omitted columns and for DEFAULT tokens, and a view column with a default that is not updatable makes `INSERT INTO rw_view15 (a) VALUES (4)` fail `cannot insert into column "upper" of view "rw_view15"` DETAIL 'View columns that are not columns of their base relation are not updatable.'; with an INSTEAD OF trigger or unconditional DO INSTEAD rule, columns without a view default become NULL (not the table default); a DO ALSO rule inserts each row twice (base_tab_def 22 rows).
roots.what_gres_does: `syntax error at position 20: unsupported ALTER VIEW subcommand, found Ident("alter"); expected OWNER TO, SET (…) or RESET (…)`; every subsequent INSERT through the view uses table defaults ('Unspecified' / 'Table default'), so base_tab_def blocks differ (4 x 32 lines + 59).

Persist the per-view-column default
Apply view defaults before mapping to base columns; a defaulted non-base column becomes an insert refusal
NULLs for columns without a view default when a trigger takes over

roots.title: Privilege checks through views: column-level grants, view-vs-base attribution, security_invoker, ON CONFLICT
roots.what_pg_does: `GRANT UPDATE (a, c) ON base_tbl` admits `UPDATE base_tbl SET a=a, c=c` and `UPDATE rw_view1 SET bb=bb, cc=cc` through the view's mapping; the error names the first relation whose check fails in rangetable order (view first, then the base relation the rewriter added): `permission denied for view rw_view1` when the view's own grant is missing, `permission denied for table base_tbl` when the view owner (or invoker for security_invoker) lacks the base grant; MERGE follows the same rules per action; INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE through a view checks UPDATE on the assigned view columns (`set cc = 3.0` -> `permission denied for view rw_view1`).
roots.what_gres_does: privilege.rs stores column grants but never admits by them ('a role holding only column grants is refused the relation outright'), so `UPDATE base_tbl SET a=a, c=c; -- ok` errors; view-over-view cases name the wrong relation (`permission denied for view rw_view1` where PG says `table base_tbl` and vice versa); ON CONFLICT via view skips the check (`set cc = 3.0` succeeds; base_tbl shows c=3).

roots.title: Auto-updatable view rewrite: correlated quals, check-option subqueries, inheritance, INSTEAD OF RETURNING, PREPARE, error attribution
roots.what_pg_does: UPDATE/DELETE through a view whose WHERE holds a correlated subquery (`EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM t2 WHERE t2.cc = v1.c)`, `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM t12 WHERE t12.a = t1.a)`) rewrites onto the base relation keeping the alias, so it works; WITH CHECK OPTION quals with subqueries are evaluated per new row (`new row violates check option for view "rw_view1"` DETAIL `Failing row contains (15).`); a view over an inheritance parent updates/deletes children too unless ONLY; INSTEAD OF trigger views return all view columns in RETURNING old.*/new.* (incl. constant c2 of the outer view); `PREPARE ins(int, int[]) AS INSERT INTO rw_view1 VALUES($1, $2)` works; column refusal names the outer view's own computed column first (`cannot insert into column "t" of view "rw_view2"`) and system columns get DETAIL 'View columns that refer to system columns are not updatable.'; the rewritten WHERE is evaluated once per row and, for security_barrier views, the view qual before the caller's qual.

roots.title: Leaky-function evaluation order for plain vs security_barrier views
roots.what_pg_does: A non-barrier view is flattened and quals ordered by cost, so `f_leak(passwd)` (COST 0.0000001) runs on every base row before `name = CURRENT_USER` (3 NOTICEs); a security_barrier view runs the view qual first (1 NOTICE); joins evaluate the leaky qual once per inner row (Materialize); UPDATE/DELETE follow the same placement.
roots.what_gres_does: Always materialises the view body then applies the caller's qual (1 NOTICE for non-barrier); the join case prints 5 NOTICEs (per join output row).

fix_location.symbol: view scan / build_from_schema_of_select (view body materialisation) and qual application
fix_location.why: Flatten simple views and order quals by cost unless security_barrier
Show flattened base scans (planner-only for exactness)

roots.size_rationale: Requires view inlining and cost-ordered qual evaluation, which is planner territory; only the NOTICE lines are non-planner.
roots.evidence: select_views.diff H3 (`-NOTICE: f_leak => beafsteak / hamburger`), H10 (extra `+NOTICE: f_leak => 1111-2222-3333-4444` x4), updatable_views H85/H89.

brief_corrections: select_into is not a small standalone file: Gres executes `INSERT INTO int4_tbl SELECT 1 INTO f;` (PG errors 42601 'SELECT ... INTO is not allowed here'), so int4_tbl carries an extra row `1` for every later test in the serial schedule (join, subselect, union, join_hash, aggregates, ...). ~140 lines of this cluster (join ~80, subselect ~37, union 13, join_hash 7) are that pollution, plus an unknown number in other clusters. One-line parser fix; do it first.

join_hash is a whole-file cascade (704 of 843 lines) on `update pg_class set reltuples = ...` -> 'relation "pg_catalog.pg_class" does not exist' inside the file's `begin;`. The brief's '20 gres-error lines' undercounts: 241 +ERROR lines.

select_parallel (1148 lines) is a whole-file cascade on `select sp_test_func() order by 1;` (SQL SETOF function in the select list) inside a file-wide `begin; ... rollback;`; 199 +ERROR lines, not 20. explain (693) is likewise a cascade on plpgsql SETOF `explain_filter()` in the select list AND on `\m`/`\M` regex escapes inside its body; the EXPLAIN option/format gaps only surface after both are fixed. memoize loses 226 of 308 the same way.

The largest non-planner engine defect in the cluster is not in the brief: a fixed 16 MiB blocking-query memory budget (crates/pgexec/src/scanner.rs BLOCKING_QUERY_MEMORY, charged as size_of::<Datum>() per column) makes tenk1 (10000 rows x 16 cols) unsortable/unjoinable and the 20000-row abbrev_abort_uuids unsortable: 46 statements / ~830 lines (tuplesort 438, join ~190, limit ~70, memoize 54, tidscan 18, subselect ~20) fail with '53200 blocking query exceeded the memory budget'. PostgreSQL spills; it never errors.

predicate, equivclass and a ~600-line slice of join are dominated by rule-based planner transformations (qual distribution to base scans, NullTest reduction to One-Time Filter: false, X=X -> IS NOT NULL, useless-join removal, self-join elimination, subquery pull-up, sublink pull-up) rather than cost-based choices; these should be planned as a separate work item from the cost model.

tidrangescan and most of tidscan do NOT require a cost-based planner: a rule (single-relation plan whose quals include ctid =/IN/range -> Tid [Range] Scan with TID Cond) plus typed constant deparse ('(0,1)'::tid, not ::text) matches them; the remaining tidscan lines are tid[] arrays (parser), WHERE CURRENT OF (parser), Hash/Merge join blocks (planner) and SERIALIZABLE.

The prior triage's join breakdown (3,585 EXPLAIN / 2,010 content / 1,186 rulers / 450 ordering / 182 error) does not match this artifact: ~1,900 lines are cross-join row order (planner join order), 4,461 explain-hunk lines, 1,552 error-block lines, and only ~75 lines are genuinely wrong row content (int4_tbl pollution + one lateral name-precedence bug).
`WITHIN GROUP` (ordered-set / hypothetical-set aggregates) is not parsed at all (grep within_group crates/pgparser -> nothing); tuplesort loses 12 lines to it. Belongs to agg_window.

roots.title: Cost-based planner (path selection, join order/method, index/bitmap/tid access, Materialize/Memoize/Sort/Incremental Sort/parallel) with a faithful EXPLAIN renderer and matching executor
roots.what_pg_does: Chooses Seq/Index/Index Only/Bitmap/Tid scans, Hash/Merge/Nested Loop (+Semi/Anti/Left/Right/Full) joins and join order by cost from pg_class.reltuples/relpages + pg_statistic; places Materialize/Memoize/Sort/Incremental Sort/Unique/Limit/Gather/Gather Merge/Parallel */Merge Append/HashSetOp/SetOp; EXPLAIN prints exactly those nodes plus Index Cond/Recheck Cond/Hash Cond/Merge Cond/Cache Key/Cache Mode/Presorted Key/Workers Planned; EXPLAIN ANALYZE prints per-node actual rows/loops, Sort Method, Memoize Hits/Misses/Evictions/Memory Usage, Heap Fetches, Index Searches, Rows Removed by Filter, Disabled: true. Unsorted result row order follows the chosen plan (nested-loop outer/inner choice, hash build side, merge-join sorting, index-scan order under enable_seqscan=off).
roots.what_gres_does: crates/pgexec/src/explain.rs is a syntactic AST walk: every join prints 'Nested Loop', every scan 'Seq Scan', no ON-clause Join Filter, no Materialize/Memoize/Index/Bitmap/Tid/Hash/Merge nodes, no parallel nodes; the executor never consults secondary indexes for ordinary scans and joins in FROM order (hash-index probe when a hashable equality key exists), so cross-join and merge-join row orders differ (join hunks 0-38: ~1,900 lines).

fix_location.why: the whole renderer must be driven by a plan IR instead of the AST

fix_location.why: no planner exists today; needs reltuples/relpages/pg_statistic and the enable_*/work_mem/parallel GUCs already stored in session.rs (~1100-1300)
executor must run the chosen join method (hash/merge/nested loop, semi/anti) and expose per-node instrumentation
ANALYZE counts only the root result rows today; per-node actuals need executor instrumentation

roots.size_rationale: Requires a real planner (statistics, cost model, join search, pathkeys, parallel plan shapes) plus executor support for the chosen paths and instrumentation; multi-week subsystem.

roots.notes: ~2,300 of the attributable lines are behind cascade producers (join_hash pg_class, select_parallel/explain/memoize SRF). Under whole-block attribution these blocks also carry the non-planner defects listed in the next four roots, which must land first or together.

roots.title: Rule-based planner preprocessing: subquery pull-up, qual distribution, join removal, self-join elimination, sublink pull-up, NullTest/const reduction, IN-list to ScalarArrayOp, X=X to IS NOT NULL, const folding, alias numbering and Var qualification rule
roots.what_pg_does: Deterministically: pulls up simple derived tables (no 'Subquery Scan on ss'), pushes single-relation WHERE quals to the scan ('Filter:') and multi-relation quals to the join ('Join Filter:'), pushes quals into UNION ALL arms, rewrites 'x IN (1,2)' as '(x = ANY ('{1,2}'::integer[]))', 'x = x' as 'x IS NOT NULL', drops provably-true NullTests on NOT NULL columns and turns provably-false ones into 'Result / One-Time Filter: false' (also 'Join Filter: false'), removes useless LEFT JOINs to unique inners and self-joins (SJE), pulls EXISTS/IN sublinks up to semi/anti joins, folds single-row VALUES to Result, inlines non-materialized CTEs, folds immutable calls (point(5,5) -> '(5,5)'::point, random()*.1 -> (random() * '0.1'::double precision)), numbers duplicate aliases (tenk1_1, t_1, "*VALUES*_1", unnamed_subquery), qualifies Vars when the plan has more than one RTE (s.x, t.a), flattens AND/OR lists.
roots.what_gres_does: explain.rs::plan_from puts the entire WHERE on the topmost join as 'Join Filter: (((a AND b) AND c) AND d)', prints 'Subquery Scan on s' for every derived table, 'Filter: (t.a IN (1, 2))', 'Filter: ((unique1 = unique1) AND ...)', keeps NullTests, never removes joins, prints 'Seq Scan on ec1' three times without _1/_2/_3, prints 'Filter: (ctid <= ctid)' for a lateral outer reference.

fix_location.symbol: pull_up_subqueries / distribute_qual_to_rels / remove_useless_joins / reduce_outer_joins / eval_const_expressions equivalents
fix_location.why: these are the non-cost half of PG's planner and are prerequisites for every plan block

brief_corrections: file_stats.json error_lines differ from the brief (aggregates 175 not 60, with 161 not 100, rangefuncs 235 not 60, polymorphism 144, rowtypes 127, tsrf 44, create_aggregate 56, functional_deps 18, window 58, groupingsets 34); the brief's 'explain-ish' counts undercount window (WindowAgg is missing from Gres EXPLAIN entirely: 595 window lines are explain hunks) and overcount groupingsets/aggregates slightly (some 'explain-ish' lines are result-order changes).

The brief says the read path 'prints every join as Nested Loop' — true, but the dominant non-planner defect in window (1198 lines) is row emission order after windowing plus unstable-qsort tie order, not planning.

Several failures in this cluster are cross-file contamination, not local defects: select_into's `INSERT INTO int4_tbl SELECT 1 INTO f` succeeds in Gres and leaves int4_tbl with 6 rows (aggregates, with, polymorphism show an extra `1` row); create_aggregate failures (builtin sfuncs, aggtype[]) cascade into aggregates/polymorphism.
CREATE RULE is a matrix Non-goal but costs 174 lines in with; the brief asks to size everything so it is listed as a root (agg_window-rules-nongoal).

The brief lists rangefuncs/polymorphism/rowtypes under 'agg_window' but their roots are routine/type-system roots (SQL-function executor, user function scans, table rowtypes, arrays of any type, generic operator lexing) shared with other clusters; they are reported here with fix locations but should be owned once.

The 'blocking query exceeded the memory budget' errors are a harness/engine capacity setting (scanner.rs BLOCKING_QUERY_MEMORY 16MiB, scripts/gres-pg-regress.sh 20MiB), not a semantic gap; they abort transaction blocks and cascade.

files.name: aggregates
files.first_failing_statement: SELECT any_value(v) FROM (VALUES (1), (2), (3)) AS v (v);
files.notes: Local cascades: create_aggregate failures poison newavg/newsum/aggfns/agg_view1 blocks (attributed to builtin-support-functions and arrays-of-any-type); `begin work` parse failure runs a block outside a transaction so my_sum persists and later CREATE fails; memory-budget error aborts the parallel-agg txn block (27 cascade lines). Extra int4_tbl row (1) from select_into contamination adds 6 lines. Attribution: PLANNER 706, ordered-set 244, arrays 181, builtin sfuncs 140, agg overloads 104, outer-level 75, plpgsql 60, view-bytea 51, lexer 41, memory 36, colname 30, useragg 27, errpos 17, grouped-order 14, misc 34.

files.name: groupingsets
files.first_failing_statement: select a, b, grouping(a,b), sum(v), count(*), max(v) from gstest1 group by rollup (a,b);
files.notes: 731 lines are `a | ?column?` header/width changes because a lateral outer column ref (`select v.a, ...` in a LATERAL subquery) is named ?column? (whole 70-row result blocks re-flow). Rollup emission order (59) is deterministic sort-based subtotal order; the cube/mixed-hash orders (H1, 4 lines) are counted as planner. gstest_data(v.x) (plpgsql OUT-param setof record with lateral args) fails 'column definition list is required' → user-function-scans 92.

files.name: window
files.first_failing_statement: SELECT depname, empno, salary, sum(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY depname) FROM empsalary ORDER BY depname, salary;
files.notes: 1198 lines: Gres emits window rows in input order; PostgreSQL emits the last WindowAgg's sort order with pg_qsort (unstable) tie order, and ORDER BY sorts on top of that also show qsort tie order (Gres sort_by is stable). 595 lines are EXPLAIN hunks where Gres prints no WindowAgg/Window:/Run Condition/Sort at all; roughly half of those need cost decisions (Sort vs Index Scan, qual pushdown into Subquery Scan, Merge Join). Frame semantics 409 (infinite interval offsets, timetz, `unbounded` param precedence, WINDOW over GROUP BY, LANGUAGE internal WINDOW fn).

roots.title: Window output ordering and pg_qsort-faithful tie order for window sorts and ORDER BY

ORDER BY on top of a window sorts the WindowAgg output with the same algorithm.

brief_corrections: Harness, not server: scripts/gres-pg-regress.sh:28 sets GRES_DB default 'crab' while the oracle uses --dbname=regression. psql compares the written database name with PQdb() client-side, so 132 lines of psql (the `\dt regression."no.such.schema".x` family, expected diff lines 6651-6790) print 'cross-database references are not implemented' purely because of the harness. Gres accepts any startup dbname (crates/pgwire/src/session.rs:1039). One-line fix: GRES_PG_REGRESS_DB=regression.
The captured Gres server.log is 4 lines long and carries no per-statement diagnostics; the triage below is from the .out files and source only.
file_stats error_lines undercounts badly: largeobject has ~99 Gres ERROR lines (not 20), type_sanity 44 (not 6), psql 103 (not 60).

'psql itself is upstream, so every divergence is server-side' is not entirely true: 132 lines are the harness dbname, and 87 lines (AUTOCOMMIT off + `\;` batches, expected 5884-6025) start with `relation "foo" already exists` on the very first CREATE TABLE foo of the run; static reading of session.rs simple_query_batch_into/run_ddl/catalog_undo did not reveal the cause -- it needs a live reproduction (see root catalog_psql-autocommit-off-batch-ddl).

The `blocking query exceeded the memory budget` (53200) error is not psql-specific: it appears in 21 result files (join 10x, tuplesort 16x, portals 5x, limit 4x ...). In this cluster it costs type_sanity 122, opr_sanity 100, psql 48 lines. Budget is 20MiB via GRES_PG_REGRESS_BLOCKING_QUERY_MEMORY; a full scan of tenk1 (10k rows) or a pg_type x pg_proc join already exceeds it.
psql's 'explain_lines 33' are not planner lines: they are `EXPLAIN EXECUTE test \gdesc` (Describe of a utility statement). Planner-only lines are 0 in all seven files.
The brief lists `\watch` and `\crosstab`; neither diverges in psql.out (psql_crosstab is a separate test not in this cluster).

`heap2` in `\dA` output is created by the earlier create_am test (CREATE ACCESS METHOD heap2 TYPE TABLE HANDLER heap_tableam_handler); its absence is the CREATE ACCESS METHOD root, not a pg_am fixture bug.

roots.title: psql AUTOCOMMIT off: `CREATE TABLE foo(s TEXT) \; ROLLBACK;` reports 'relation "foo" already exists' (cause unknown, needs repro)
roots.what_pg_does: psql sends BEGIN then the two-statement string; CREATE runs, ROLLBACK undoes it; second batch CREATE/INSERT/COMMIT succeeds; `SELECT * FROM foo` shows hello/world; ON_ERROR_ROLLBACK section then works.
roots.what_gres_does: First batch errors `ERROR:  relation "foo" already exists` although no `foo` exists (temp foo tables of earlier tests live in other sessions and later temp foo creations succeed); the transaction stays aborted through the whole AUTOCOMMIT/ON_ERROR_ROLLBACK section (87 lines) until the later `COMMIT;`.

fix_location.why: the failing shape is: explicit BEGIN (separate message) followed by a multi-statement simple query whose first statement is DDL and whose last is ROLLBACK; something in that path executes or checks CREATE TABLE twice or resolves `foo` against a stale/temp namespace
alternative hypothesis: leaked temp namespace visible to CREATE's duplicate check

roots.size_rationale: Unknown cause; reproduce with `psql -v AUTOCOMMIT=off` sending `BEGIN` then `CREATE TABLE foo(s text) \; ROLLBACK;` after running select/subselect/inherit tests in earlier sessions.
roots.evidence: gres psql.out 5665-5671: `CREATE TABLE foo(s TEXT) \;` / `ROLLBACK;` / `ERROR:  relation "foo" already exists` then every following statement `current transaction is aborted`.
roots.oracle_facts: After the section: `\echo '# final AUTOCOMMIT:' :AUTOCOMMIT` etc; DROP TABLE bla; DROP FUNCTION psql_error succeed.
roots.notes: Cascade also hides psql_error() plpgsql CONTEXT lines ('PL/pgSQL function psql_error(text) line 3 at RAISE') which belong to catalog_psql-plpgsql-context-lines once unblocked.

roots.title: Blocking-query memory budget (20MiB) aborts catalog joins and tenk1 scans
roots.what_pg_does: Any size result; type_sanity/opr_sanity pg_type x pg_proc self-joins return (0 rows) or small lists; psql `select unique2 from tenk1 order by unique2 limit 19` with FETCH_COUNT 10 returns 19 rows and `select 1/(15-unique2) from tenk1 order by unique2 limit 19` returns 10 rows then `ERROR: division by zero` (22012).
roots.what_gres_does: `ERROR:  blocking query exceeded the memory budget` (53200) from scanner::collect_cursor_bounded / join.rs push_bounded_join_row when materialised rows exceed pgexec_blocking_query_memory (harness passes 20MiB; scanner::BLOCKING_QUERY_MEMORY default 16MiB). tenk1 full scans and pg_proc x pg_type nested loops exceed it because joins and sorts materialise whole intermediate relations with wide catalog rows.

fix_location.why: project only needed columns before materialising join output; stream/nested-loop without materialising the whole product

fix_location.symbol: collect_cursor_bounded call sites (line 14247, 17295): scan projection/top-k pushdown
fix_location.why: `select unique2 from tenk1 order by unique2 limit 19` should push projection + top-K so only 19 rows are retained; the volatile-function LIMIT cases in limit.out need a streaming Sort+Limit
accounting counts size_of::<Datum> per cell (large); alternatively raise the default or the harness knob GRES_PG_REGRESS_BLOCKING_QUERY_MEMORY in scripts/gres-pg-regress.sh:267

roots.size_rationale: Cheapest exact fix is the harness knob (S) but that hides a real executor limitation; projection pushdown before join materialisation and streaming top-K is M. Shared with join/limit/portals/tuplesort clusters (21 files).

roots.title: Syntax error text: 'syntax error at or near "X"' / 'at end of input' with LINE/caret
roots.what_pg_does: `ERROR:  syntax error at or near ";"` + `LINE 1: SELECT 1 UNION;` + caret; `syntax error at end of input`; with VERBOSITY terse `syntax error at or near ";" at character 15`; :LAST_ERROR_MESSAGE holds the same text; `bogus;` -> `syntax error at or near "bogus"`.
roots.what_gres_does: `syntax error at position 14: expected Keyword(Select), found Semicolon`, `syntax error at position 11: unexpected token Eof`, `syntax error at position 0: unexpected statement start Ident("bogus")`, no LINE/caret (ParseError::new formats the message with the byte position and reports_position=false).

fix_location.why: message must be `syntax error at or near "<source text of the offending token>"` or `syntax error at end of input`, position reported as the 1-based char offset (P field) so psql draws LINE/caret; drop the internal token-kind text
ParseError needs the token's source text (quote_identifier-free raw spelling) at the failure position
propagate the reported position to PgError.position

roots.size_rationale: Central change in ParseError plus every hand-written `ParseError::new("expected ...")` message; large cross-cluster payoff (every syntax error in the schedule).
roots.evidence: diff psql 881-940, 1554; expected 4837 `ERROR:  syntax error at or near ";"` / `LINE 1: SELECT 1 UNION;` / caret at column 23.
roots.oracle_facts: SQLSTATE 42601; terse form appends ` at character N`; :LAST_ERROR_MESSAGE is the message without LINE.
roots.notes: Shared with the errors cluster; also unblocks `SELECT 1 + \gdesc` and `SELECT 4 AS \gdesc` ('syntax error at end of input').

roots.title: Extended-protocol pipeline implicit transaction block (until Sync)
roots.what_pg_does: Statements executed via Parse/Bind/Execute without an intervening Sync run in one implicit transaction block: BEGIN inside converts it to explicit; ROLLBACK undoes earlier pipelined INSERTs; the block commits at Sync; after an error the rest is skipped until Sync; REINDEX CONCURRENTLY/VACUUM/CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY raise `X cannot run inside a transaction block` when not the first command; LOCK/SAVEPOINT raise `can only be used in transaction blocks` when first; SET LOCAL warns only when first; `\getresults` after `\flushrequest` returns results of the pipelined statements.
roots.what_gres_does: Each Execute autocommits (SqlSession::sync only clears portals; no XACT_FLAGS_PIPELINING equivalent), so INSERT 1 of the 'implicit->explicit' pipeline persists, the next pipeline hits duplicate key, its explicit BEGIN stays aborted, and 142 lines cascade; LOCK inside a pipeline says `LOCK TABLE can only be used in transaction blocks`; VACUUM/REINDEX CONCURRENTLY do not complain when not first.

fix_location.symbol: sync() (line 16351), execute path (16240-16290), begin_implicit_transaction (3308) / implicit_transaction flag
fix_location.why: open an implicit block on the first Execute since the last Sync, keep it open across Executes, commit at Sync (or when an explicit COMMIT/ROLLBACK ends it), convert to explicit on BEGIN, abort on error until Sync
drive the session's pipeline state; keep ext.failed semantics

fix_location.symbol: PreventInTransactionBlock-style checks for VACUUM/REINDEX CONCURRENTLY/CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY/CLUSTER... and RequireTransactionBlock checks for LOCK/SAVEPOINT/SET LOCAL warning

roots.size_rationale: Transaction lifecycle change in the session core with subtle rules; interacts with autocommit DDL and read-only checks.

brief_corrections: insert_conflict '~166 explain-ish' and merge '~218 explain-ish' are almost entirely missing EXPLAIN *renderer* output (Conflict Resolution / Conflict Arbiter Indexes / Conflict Filter lines, 'Merge on t' node, VERBOSE Output lines, JSON 'ModifyTable' + 'Operation'), not planner choice; the planner-only remainder is ~5 (insert_conflict) and ~58 (merge). Gres EXPLAIN of MERGE prints just 'Result' (explain.rs plan_statement has no Merge arm).

update '~0 explain-ish' is wrong: 49 changed lines are EXPLAIN (VERBOSE UPDATE with Result/One-Time Filter/SubPlan; partitioned UPDATE Append with per-partition 'Update on partN range_parted_N' lines) and are planner-only.

copy2 '40 gres-error lines': there are 102 +ERROR lines and the biggest cost (132 lines) is a single root (COPY FROM cannot run plpgsql row triggers: 'trigger function requires a session executor'), invisible in the error count.

insert '60 gres-error lines' is 259; 354 of 630 lines are one root (expression partition keys, partition.rs:1158). The same root leaks across files: create_table's multi-table DROP fails because range_parted3 (PARTITION BY RANGE (a,(b+1))) never existed, so part1..part4 survive and merge.out gets 'relation "part1" already exists' (16 lines).

Gres already supports RETURNING old.*/new.* for single-table INSERT/DELETE (returning.out rows match apart from ctid values); the gap is bare whole-row 'old'/'new', old/new inside RETURNING subqueries, MERGE RETURNING old/new + merge_action() nested in expressions, and partitioned targets.

session.rs precheck_copy_from asserts 'cannot copy to view' must be raised before CopyInResponse; PostgreSQL raises it in CopyFrom() after ReceiveCopyBegin (copy2 expected shows no leaked 'test1' data line), whereas 'column "d" specified more than once' must be raised BEFORE CopyInResponse and today is raised after (Gres consumed the following comment + COPY statement as data).

Gres UPDATE keeps the row's rowid (apply_locked_row_update writes a new version under the same rowid), so an updated row keeps its scan position; PostgreSQL's new heap tuple sorts after the existing rows. This is why 'SELECT * FROM t' after UPDATE / ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE / MERGE UPDATE differs in insert_conflict, merge, and returning (36 lines incl. ctid values) — it is a storage-order emulation gap, not a planner gap.

The MERGE 'invalid reference to FROM-clause entry for table t' test is not inside a transaction: Gres accepts the target reference in a NOT MATCHED INSERT and inserts a persistent (NULL,40) row that contaminates ~40 later result blocks in merge.out (all attributed to dml-merge-clause-scope-visibility).

roots.title: Expression partition keys (PARTITION BY ... ((b+0)) / (lower(a)) / (abs(b)))
roots.what_pg_does: Accepts arbitrary expressions in the partition key, coerces bounds to the expression's result type, routes rows by evaluating the expression, reports 'no partition of relation "range_parted" found for row' + 'DETAIL: Partition key of the failing row contains (a, (b + 0)) = (a, 11).' (omitting the DETAIL when the key contains an expression the user cannot see or lacks SELECT on all key columns), validates bounds ('every bound following MINVALUE must also be MINVALUE' + LINE caret), and prints 'Partition key: LIST (lower(a))' in \d+.
roots.what_gres_does: ERROR (0A000): expression partition keys are not supported: PARTITION BY … ((b+0)) needs the expression's result type to coerce partition bounds against ... — every dependent CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION OF, INSERT, UPDATE and \d+ then fails with 'relation does not exist'; in create_table the same refusal makes the multi-table DROP fail so part1..part4 leak into merge.out.

roots.title: MERGE into partitioned tables

roots.what_gres_does: ERROR: MERGE into a partitioned table is not supported: a source row that matches no target row would have to be routed, and the matched/not-matched decision spans every partition at once

brief_corrections: file_stats.json has no entry for prepared_xacts_1 (the variant file); its diff is 286 changed lines in one hunk.
The rough classifier's gres-error counts are far off: portals has 205 '+ERROR' lines (brief says 30), transactions 71 (brief 40), sequence 128 (brief 40).

The brief frames EXPLAIN gaps as plan choice; in fast_default the 68 EXPLAIN lines are mostly EXPLAIN VERBOSE renderer work (missing 'Output:' lines, schema-qualified 'Seq Scan on fast_default.t', 't.col' qualification in Sort Key/Filter, '-1'::integer literal rendering, BETWEEN expanded to two comparisons); only the DELETE block (16 lines) needs a Bitmap Heap/Index Scan plan.

docs/PG_COMPAT_MATRIX.md 'ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT' row says a sub-transaction that changed rows cannot be undone (0A000); transactions.out shows those blocks now match apart from xmin, so the row is stale.

docs/PG_COMPAT_MATRIX.md 'BEGIN'/'SET TRANSACTION' rows imply READ ONLY / DEFERRABLE modes are handled everywhere; crates/pgparser/src/parser.rs set_transaction_tail() carries only the isolation level, so SET TRANSACTION READ WRITE inside a READ ONLY block is silently accepted and SET SESSION CHARACTERISTICS AS TRANSACTION READ ONLY does nothing.

docs/PG_COMPAT_MATRIX.md 'DECLARE' row says materialization at DECLARE is a faithful INSENSITIVE implementation; the oracle shows three observable differences (error at FETCH not DECLARE, 'portal X cannot be run' after a failed FETCH in a rolled-back subtransaction, volatile functions inside the cursor see rows inserted after DECLARE).

The pg_regress harness (scripts/gres-pg-regress.sh, GRES_DB default 'crab') runs against a database named crab, not regression, so every printed database name (information_schema.*_catalog, current_database()) differs from the oracle; this is a harness fix, not an engine fix.
prepared_xacts: the cheapest exact match is NOT 2PC; exposing max_prepared_transactions=0 makes psql \quit and the _1 variant matches byte-for-byte.

Three of my files (identity, fast_default) plus alter_table show that DROP TABLE never drops the serial/identity-owned sequence (a re-CREATE of the same table name fails with 'sequence "t_id_seq" already exists'); this is not documented anywhere as a divergence and costs 152 lines here.

roots.title: SET TRANSACTION / SESSION CHARACTERISTICS access mode and deferrable, RESET guards, AND CHAIN copies all characteristics
roots.what_pg_does: SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY|READ WRITE|[NOT] DEFERRABLE change the open block (25001 'transaction read-write mode must be set before any query' after a query; 25006 'cannot set transaction read-write mode inside a read-only transaction' when the block was started READ ONLY); SET SESSION CHARACTERISTICS AS TRANSACTION ... sets default_transaction_read_only/deferrable/isolation for later blocks and autocommit statements (DROP TABLE/INSERT/EXECUTE of an UPDATE/CREATE TABLE AS then fail 25006 'cannot execute DROP TABLE in a read-only transaction'); RESET transaction_isolation/transaction_read_only/transaction_deferrable is 55P02 'parameter "transaction_isolation" cannot be reset'; SHOW transaction_deferrable reports on for a DEFERRABLE block; COMMIT AND CHAIN / ROLLBACK AND CHAIN reopen a block with the same isolation, read-only and deferrable characteristics (not the session defaults).
roots.what_gres_does: parser.rs set_transaction_tail() emits Statement::Set{name:'__set_transaction'} carrying only the isolation level, so READ WRITE/READ ONLY/DEFERRABLE after SET TRANSACTION are dropped and SET SESSION CHARACTERISTICS is treated as SET TRANSACTION; RESET of the transaction_* GUCs succeeds; TxnCtx has no deferrable field so SHOW transaction_deferrable is off; chained_isolation() passes only IsolationLevel and open_chained_block() calls begin(Some(level), None) which re-reads default_transaction_read_only (so a READ WRITE block chained under default_transaction_read_only=on becomes read-only and 'INSERT INTO trans_abc VALUES (4)' fails 25006).

fix_location.why: carry read_only and deferrable in the AST for SET TRANSACTION and produce a distinct statement for SET SESSION CHARACTERISTICS AS TRANSACTION

fix_location.symbol: set_transaction, begin, TxnCtx, chained_isolation, open_chained_block, reset_guc
fix_location.why: apply/refuse access-mode changes with 25001/25006, add deferrable to TxnCtx and SHOW, chain all three characteristics, guard RESET of transaction_* GUCs with 55P02

roots.evidence: transactions.diff H4/H7/H21-H28: '-ERROR:  transaction read-write mode must be set before any query' vs '+ERROR:  current transaction is aborted'; 'SHOW transaction_deferrable  - on  + off'; 'INSERT INTO trans_abc VALUES (4);  +ERROR:  cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction' after COMMIT AND CHAIN of a READ WRITE block.
roots.oracle_facts: 25001 'transaction read-write mode must be set before any query'; 25006 'cannot set transaction read-write mode inside a read-only transaction'; 25006 'cannot execute <TAG> in a read-only transaction' with TAG = DROP TABLE, INSERT, UPDATE (via EXECUTE), CREATE TABLE AS; 55P02 'parameter "transaction_isolation" cannot be reset'; SHOW transaction_deferrable -> on/off; chained block keeps isolation/read_only/deferrable.

roots.title: Accept SERIALIZABLE isolation (run as REPEATABLE READ, report 'serializable')
roots.what_pg_does: BEGIN/START TRANSACTION/SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL SERIALIZABLE succeed; SHOW transaction_isolation prints serializable; default_transaction_isolation = serializable makes plain BEGIN serializable.
roots.what_gres_does: session.rs require_supported_isolation() refuses with 0A000 'SERIALIZABLE isolation level is not implemented; serialization anomalies would go undetected', which aborts the block and cascades (transactions 3 sites, portals 1, vacuum 1, prepared_xacts 6 sites).

fix_location.why: map Serializable onto the RR snapshot path and report 'serializable'; single-session pg_regress cannot observe the missing SSI

roots.title: Multi-statement simple Query is an implicit transaction block
roots.what_pg_does: All statements of one simple-protocol Query string ('a\; b\; c') run in one implicit transaction: an error rolls back the earlier statements' effects; COMMIT/ROLLBACK inside it commit/abort and raise WARNING 'there is no transaction in progress'; BEGIN inside converts it to a real block; VACUUM inside is 25001 'VACUUM cannot run inside a transaction block'; SAVEPOINT is 25P01 'SAVEPOINT can only be used in transaction blocks'; COMMIT AND CHAIN is 25P01.
roots.what_gres_does: session.rs simple_query()/simple_query_batch_into() run each parsed statement with run_one_with_source independently, so 'insert into i_table values(2)\; select 1/0' leaves row 2 committed, VACUUM inside runs, and the WARNINGs are missing (rows 2, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 18, 20 wrongly present).

fix_location.why: open an implicit block when a Query holds >1 statement, treat COMMIT/ROLLBACK/BEGIN/VACUUM/SAVEPOINT per PG rules, roll back on error

roots.title: Command-id visibility: volatile functions called by a statement see that statement's earlier writes
roots.what_pg_does: In 'update xacttest set a = max_xacttest() + 10 where a > 0', a VOLATILE SQL or plpgsql max_xacttest() takes a fresh snapshot per call (CommandCounterIncrement) and sees rows already updated by the same UPDATE (results 787, 797, 807, 817); a STABLE one sees the statement's snapshot (all 787).
roots.what_gres_does: Volatile SQL functions read the outer statement's snapshot: all four rows become 787.

fix_location.why: a volatile body must run with a snapshot that includes the calling command's writes so far (command-id aware visibility) instead of the outer statement's fixed snapshot
expose the current command id and the rows the running command has written to nested reads

roots.title: Cursors execute lazily at first FETCH under the DECLARE-time snapshot; failed portals become 'cannot be run'
roots.what_pg_does: DECLARE only plans; the first FETCH runs the query with the snapshot taken at DECLARE (stable functions see it, volatile functions see later inserts: count_tt1_v()=2, count_tt1_s()=1); a FETCH that errors inside a savepoint leaves the portal failed: after ROLLBACK TO, FETCH is 55000 'portal "c" cannot be run'; DECLARE ctt CURSOR FOR SELECT create_temp_tab() does not raise the plpgsql error until FETCH ctt (with CONTEXT lines).
