brief_corrections: foreign_key is not '~0 explain-ish': it has one EXPLAIN (a rule test) whose 8 Index Scan lines are planner-only; and plpgsql has ~45 planner-only lines (EXPLAIN Gather, Function Scan verbose, Named Tuplestore Scan INFO), so foreign_key and plpgsql cannot be byte-exact without the planner.

The brief lists 'WITHOUT OVERLAPS temporal primary/unique keys' as work: WITHOUT OVERLAPS PK/UNIQUE creation and enforcement already work in Gres; the without_overlaps file fails on format_type ('-' for range types, 136 lines) and on PERIOD foreign keys (250 lines).

The brief says 'foreign keys (partitioned tables — declared unsupported)': in addition, an FK on a plain table REFERENCING a partitioned PK is accepted but never finds rows stored in partitions (bug, ~94 lines), which is a separate root.

The plpgsql cascade is not a 'char type comparison' gap in the evaluator (eval.rs already trims bpchar operands): PL/pgSQL loses the declared column type of NEW/OLD fields (plpgsql.rs rewrite_record_field), so the trim never triggers.
Domain over composite is refused by usertype.rs (executor), not the parser; arrays of user types are refused by the parser because pgtypes' ElemType is a closed enum.
PG_COMPAT_MATRIX still says 'ALTER CONSTRAINT is not in the grammar'; parser.rs 4192 has alter_constraint_action and the exec refuses only ENFORCED/NOT VALID.
triggers.out hunks 42-47 (52 lines) are a cross-file leak from create_table.out (a leftover 'parted' table), not a triggers defect.
The COPY-trigger failure is not a trigger gap: session.rs run_copy_in bypasses the scalar-runtime worker harness that every other write path uses.

Column DEFAULT is evaluated to a constant at CREATE TABLE time (exec.rs column_from_ast); this, not sequences, is why 'DEFAULT nextval(...)' fails and why domain typdefault/date defaults are refused — one shared root worth ~170 lines in this cluster.

object_address is not one function family: 604 of 691 lines are pg_get_object_address/pg_identify_object*/pg_describe_object, but 43 lines are a VALUES type-resolution bug ('types integer and regclass cannot be matched' for VALUES ('pg_class'::regclass,0,0)) and ~28 lines are schema-qualified routine creation plus non-goal object creation (publication/subscription/transform/statistics).

create_am does not need C loading: the test needs a name-to-handler alias (gist2 = gisthandler, heap2 = heap_tableam_handler) with pg_am rows, opclass/index/table/matview/partition USING <am>, relam inheritance, default_table_access_method validation and ALTER TABLE/MATVIEW SET ACCESS METHOD. Sizing it as 'non-goal' hid an L-size implementable feature.

alter_table is not one cascade: it is ~35 independent roots. Its ATTACH PARTITION half (~150 lines) is poisoned by tables leaked from create_table (list_parted2, range_parted2, part1/2/3 survive because create_table's multi-name DROP TABLE fails on range_parted3, which was never created due to the expression-partition-key refusal). Another ~30 lines come from atacc1 leaked by constraints.out.
The rough classifier's 'gres-error lines' undercounts: drop_if_exists (170 lines) is mostly MISSING NOTICE lines ('does not exist, skipping'), not errors; the same holds for ~50 lines of alter_table.

Routines carry no schema at all (crabka_pgcatalog::routine::Routine has no namespace field; catalog key is the bare identity 'name(args)'), so 'ALTER FUNCTION SET SCHEMA unsupported' is only a symptom of a larger routine-namespace root that also breaks create_function_sql (temp_func_test schema), object_address (addr_nsp.*), event_trigger (schema_two.add) and alter_table (alter1.plus1).

pg_depend in Gres holds only trigger/event-trigger rows (catalog_rel.rs::pg_depend_rows); every DROP RESTRICT/CASCADE list is ad hoc per object kind. 'dependency tracking' is therefore a subsystem (XXL), not a family of message fixes.
The brief lists 'explain_lines ~0' for alter_table; there are ~68 planner-only lines (Append with constraint exclusion over inheritance children, index-scan row order, EXPLAIN VERBOSE over a view).

brief_corrections: The harness refused to write the markdown copy at scratchpad/analysis/statistics/findings.md ('Subagents should return findings as text, not write report files'); the block-level tally scripts and tally.json ARE saved under scratchpad/analysis/statistics/ (blocks.py, classify.py, final.py, tally.json). All findings are in this structured object instead.

file_stats.json says stats/stats_ext have ~0 explain-ish lines and 100/200 gres-error lines; the real counts are: stats 54 planner-only lines (6 EXPLAIN blocks: Index Scan / Bitmap Heap Scan on test_last_scan_pkey and two BRIN bitmap plans, plus 1 check_estimated_rows), stats_ext 813 planner-only lines (762 are check_estimated_rows 'estimated' values, 51 are Merge/Hash Join plan shapes). The 'error_lines' figures undercount because Gres error blocks that replace expected result tables cost the whole block.

stats_ext is not purely a stats problem: 65 lines are the user-defined operator symbol '<<<' not lexing (the lexer is a fixed table of built-in spellings, lexer.rs::punctuation), plus ~60 lines of small parser/typing gaps (ROW(x.*), sch.tbl.*, SELECT with empty target list, INSERT..SELECT int into text column, unknown || int4range, fipshash arg typing) and 13 lines of DROP ... CASCADE notice ordering. Those belong to parser/typing/DDL clusters and are listed here only so every hunk has an owner.

The stats file exposed a genuine transaction bug outside this cluster: session.rs::end_block_commit's TxnState::Failed arm calls abort_ctx but never undo_catalog_writes(ctx.catalog_undo), while end_block_rollback does. Result: `BEGIN; CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE test_last_scan ...; INSERT ...; <error>; COMMIT;` leaves the table in place with zero rows (Gres later answers count(*)=0 where PG says 1). Any test that COMMITs a failed block after DDL is affected. Fix is a two-line change (S).

The idx_scan/last_idx_scan assertions in stats (tenk2 `st.idx_scan >= pr.idx_scan + 1`, test_last_scan idx_scan 1->2->3 through Index Scan and Bitmap scan under enable_seqscan=off) cannot pass with counters alone: they require the read path to actually execute an index scan when enable_seqscan is off. So the relation-counter root has a hard dependency on either the planner or at least an index-scan-capable read path that honours enable_seqscan/enable_indexscan/enable_bitmapscan.

The 762 check_estimated_rows lines in stats_ext are 'planner-only' under the brief's definition (COSTS-on row estimates), but they are specifically the selectivity/ndistinct ESTIMATOR (selfuncs.c, extended_stats.c, dependencies.c, mcv.c, mvdistinct.c: estimate_num_groups, clauselist_selectivity, statext_clauselist_selectivity) plus EXPLAIN ANALYZE printing rows= for the top node. That estimator can be built as part of the statistics subsystem before any path selection exists; it does not need join ordering or cost comparison. Recommend planning it as a stats-cluster deliverable ('estimator') with the planner consuming it later.

PG_COMPAT_MATRIX marks CREATE/ALTER/DROP STATISTICS as Error-with-notice(0A000) by design ('metadata nothing reads'); with everything in scope that disposition must flip to Implemented and the RefusalCommand::CreateStatistics/AlterStatistics/DropStatistics variants in pgparser/src/ast.rs must be replaced by real AST nodes.

The oracle result for `SELECT pid AS checkpointer_pid FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE backend_type = 'checkpointer' \gset` shows Gres pg_stat_activity has no auxiliary-process rows ('no rows returned for \gset'); pg_stat_io's per-backend tests need a checkpointer row there (backend_type = 'checkpointer').

brief_corrections: Brief says tsdicts has ~20 and tstypes ~30 gres-error lines; the diffs hold 96 and 60 +ERROR lines (file_stats.json agrees with the diffs, not the brief).

Brief says tsearch has ~0 explain-ish lines; tsearch has 10 EXPLAIN blocks (80 changed lines) whose expected plans are Index Scan / Bitmap Heap Scan + Bitmap Index Scan on GiST/GIN indexes wowidx/wowidx2 (file_stats.json explain_lines=78). Those 80 lines are the only planner-only lines in the cluster.

ALTER SERVER and ALTER USER MAPPING are matrix rows 'Error-with-notice(0A000)', not declared non-goals; CREATE/DROP FOREIGN DATA WRAPPER/SERVER/USER MAPPING/FOREIGN TABLE and IMPORT FOREIGN SCHEMA are matrix 'Implemented' but only the SP40 kafka_fdw grammar subset is parsed; ALTER FOREIGN DATA WRAPPER and ALTER FOREIGN TABLE are 'Wave-assigned(P5)' and are not parsed at all (raw 'unexpected token after ALTER: Keyword(Foreign)').

foreign_data is not blocked by the regress.so dummy handler: 'CREATE FUNCTION test_fdw_handler() RETURNS fdw_handler AS :regresslib LANGUAGE C' already succeeds in Gres. The blockers are grammar (318 direct parse-error lines), missing pg_foreign_* catalogs and psql \dew/\des/\deu/\det listings (613 lines), object semantics (dependencies, ownership, validator, IF EXISTS notices; 159 lines) and cascades of the never-created foreign tables (~440 lines).

publication asserts more than catalog+DDL+psql: ~150 lines are DML-time replica-identity checks ('cannot update table "x" because it does not have a replica identity and publishes updates' + HINT), row-filter and column-list validation, and DROP COLUMN dependency on a publication column list; those need executor hooks in UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE/ON CONFLICT and in ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN.

Several tsdicts statements silently 'succeed' in Gres today (ALTER TEXT SEARCH CONFIGURATION ... ALTER MAPPING / DROP MAPPING FOR not_a_token) because parser.rs::alter_text_search discards every token after the object name; they must start to fail with PG's token-type errors once mapping DDL is real.

Text search in Gres is a placeholder rather than 'remaining gaps': crates/pgtypes/src/text_search.rs (739 lines) and crates/pgexec/src/text_search_fn.rs (1357 lines) implement their own tokenizer/printer/matcher/rank/headline; there is no default parser, no dictionary templates besides simple/snowball(english), no pg_ts_parser/pg_ts_template/pg_ts_config_map. Sizing must assume a port of PostgreSQL's tsearch (wparser_def.c, tsvector.c, tsquery.c, tsvector_op.c, tsrank.c, spell.c, dict_synonym.c, dict_thesaurus.c, ts_parse.c) rather than a patch.

The 'text does not accept an argument of type unknown' / 'tsvector does not accept an argument of type tsvector' errors in tstypes are one root: text_search_fn::eval_text_search matches Datum variants and never calls crate::eval::coerce_unknown_args, so every unknown-literal argument (tsquery, text[], regconfig) fails; the same root covers 'cannot compare text and tsquery', 'operator does not exist: text <-> tsquery', 'a @@ any(''{wr,qh}'')' and 'function to_tsquery(unknown, unknown) does not exist' in FROM position (srf.rs::plan closed registry). It is 526 lines across tstypes+tsearch, the single biggest non-XL item in the cluster.

roots.title: PostgreSQL default text-search parser (23 token types) + ts_parse/ts_token_type/ts_debug + parser-driven to_tsvector/to_tsquery pipeline + pg_ts_parser/pg_ts_template/pg_ts_config_map
roots.what_pg_does: Every text-search entry point (to_tsvector, to_tsquery incl. quoted multi-word lexemes, plainto/phraseto/websearch_to_tsquery, ts_headline, ts_debug) runs the 'default' parser (wparser_def.c state machine): 23 token types (asciiword, word, numword, email, url, host, sfloat, version, hword_numpart, hword_part, hword_asciipart, blank, tag, protocol, numhword, asciihword, hword, url_path, file, float, int, uint, entity), each mapped by pg_ts_config_map to a dictionary list; positions count every non-blank token; to_tsquery('english', '''the wether'':dc & ''  sKies '':BC') gives 'wether':CD & 'sky':BC; to_tsquery('english', '''New York''') gives 'new' <-> 'york'; ts_token_type('default') returns 23 rows (tokid, alias, description); ts_parse('default', text) returns (tokid, token) rows including blanks; ts_debug(regconfig,text) returns (alias, description, token, dictionaries regdictionary[], dictionary regdictionary, lexemes text[]) with NULL lexemes for unmapped tokens and {} for stop words; NOTICE 'text-search query doesn't contain lexemes: ""' from to_tsquery('') and NOTICE 'text-search query contains only stop words or doesn't contain lexemes, ignored' from websearch/plainto; catalogs pg_ts_parser (oid 3722 'default', prsstart/prstoken/prsend/prsheadline/prslextype regproc), pg_ts_template (simple, synonym, ispell, thesaurus, snowball), pg_ts_config_map rows for simple/english and every built-in config.
